title: Lifting compatible shifted line orientations in strict coefficient towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$. Use strict semilinear coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], their Grothendieck abelian category with exact evaluations and canonical derived reduction maps [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], and its ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L_\bullet$ be a tower of locally free rank-one $R_{n,T}$-module sheaves with transitions $q^L_{n,m}$ such that $L_n\otimes_{R_n}R_m\to L_m$ is an isomorphism for all $m\leq n$; locally free rank one means locally isomorphic to $R_{n,T}$. Let $V\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, let $s\in\mathbf Z$, and suppose there are derived isomorphisms $a_n:L_n[s]\xrightarrow{\sim}V_n$ whose reduction squares commute:
$$\rho^V_{n,m}\circ(a_n)_{R_m}=a_m\circ q^L_{n,m}[s],$$
where $q^L$ on this formula denotes the induced scalar-extension map and derived scalar extension is [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Then $V[-s]$ has cohomology only in degree zero. Put $W_\bullet=H^0(V[-s])$ with its induced strict transitions $t^W_{n,m}$, and use the canonical single-degree identification $W_\bullet[0]\simeq V[-s]$. Each $a_n[-s]$ corresponds to a unique sheaf isomorphism $\alpha_n:L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}W_n$, and
$$t^W_{n,m}\circ\alpha_n=\alpha_m\circ q^L_{n,m},\qquad
\alpha_m^{-1}\circ t^W_{n,m}=q^L_{n,m}\circ\alpha_n^{-1}.$$
Thus these sheaf maps give an isomorphism $\alpha:L_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}W_\bullet$, whose shift and the single-degree identification give an isomorphism $a:L_\bullet[s]\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ evaluating to each prescribed $a_n$.

proof.text: For K=V[-s], exact evaluation and shift cancellation identify ev_n(K) with L_n[0]. The canonical exact-derived homology comparison shows every evaluation of H^i(K) is zero for i≠0. Faithfulness of A.equivalence.functor and componentwise extensionality prove id_{H^i K}=0. Apply the standard concentration theorem. For K≅Y[0], use the induced H^0(K)≅Y to obtain j:H^0(K)[0]≅K; naturality of singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso proves its required normalization.

Set W=H^0(K) and J=shiftedIdentification(j). The composite a_n, then ev_n(J^{-1}), then the evaluation single/shift comparison is an isomorphism L_n[0][s]≅W_n[0][s]. Lift it through the fully faithful composite singleFunctor ⋙ shiftFunctor to obtain beta_n. The map_preimage identity proves its prescribed level equation. Naturality of A.reduction at J^{-1} transports the assumed reduction square to these shifted single maps. Apply lem-sp-shifted-single-reduction-detects-transition to obtain the actual strict transition equations for beta_n.

Make the strict map f with components beta_n and the compatibility just proved. Componentwise invertibility makes f invertible. Lift asIso(f) through the equivalence to alpha:L≅W; map_preimage identifies its components with beta_n. Faithfulness of singleFunctor ⋙ shiftFunctor and cancellation of the evaluation comparison and ev_n(J) prove the required iff for arbitrary beta. The forward and inverse strict transition identities are the comm fields of the images of alpha.hom and alpha.inv. Finally let b=alpha[0][s] followed by J. Naturality of the exact-evaluation single and shift comparisons, followed by the defining level equation of beta_n, proves ev_n(b)=a_n in the stated normalization.
